name: The Trial Domes
hours: Four small domed duel rooms (Dome 1–4), bookable for ranked ladder matches, exams and practicums; open Morning to Evening. Ranked results are signed at the ladder registrar's table (Zeynep Arslan, Midday); Gani Villaluz checks the tables each Morning.
sight: Four white geodesic domes stand in a row like half-buried golf balls, each with a brass number over the door. Inside, a single holo-table stands on a round dais under a lattice of projectors, with a judge's chair, a score clock and two rows of benches for witnesses. The acoustics are odd: a whisper at the table reaches the back wall. It smells of ozone and floor polish.
things: Book a dome for a ranked ladder duel at the terminal by Dome 1
Sit on the witness bench for someone else's match
Play your Placement Duel (Day 1) or a practical exam here
Read the booking sheet to see who has been grinding
Watch the projector lattice warm up: a drizzle of test pixels falling onto the table
Take the Table Practicum on Wednesdays and Fridays
Check the 'matches of the week' clips looping on the screen outside
secret: Placement Duel Day 1; Table Practicum (cp150); ranked ladder matches; Promotion Duels Days 89–91. DOME 3: Brant Kessler is found here at dawn on Day 40, sitting upright at the table, eyes open. The school says seizure. Details for an attentive player: the score clock is stopped at 02:10; the dais is rimed with a ring of melting frost; Brant's deck box is open and the cards he extorted from Commons kids are stacked neatly on the opponent's side, sorted by owner. The booking sheet shows a formal challenge entry in very tidy handwriting, ante column filled in with two words that have been blacked out by the Chancellor's office before lunch. From D40 Dome 3 is closed 'for recalibration'; its door seal is tape, not a lock. Holograms projected in Dome 3 afterwards flicker toward the north. ACCESS NOTE: Dome 3 sealed from Day 40. All domes locked at night; from Day 67 bookings end with the Afternoon slot.
